newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber ends up on Tokyo, covering.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber ends up on Tokyo, covering.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed higher, maintaining their uptrend as sentiment was helped by a strong performance in Tokyo futures market, shortcovering by dealers and rains in growing areas.
"There's still a lot of shortcovering going on, especially for SMR20," said one dealer. "I believe the market still has room to move up."

She said rains in northern growing areas since the weekend were beginning to put slight pressure on production and supply of raw materials. The Meteorological Services Department said it expected heavy rains this week.

At the close, benchmark September RSS1 buyer was quoted at 328.50 cents ($1.32) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, up two cents from Tuesday. September SMR20 buyer was also up two cents at 310.50 cents ($1.25) a kg.
Rates offered by trading houses were also generally marked up. The SMR20 was offered at 310 cents, SMR10 at 311, SMR5 at 324, SMR CV at 378, SMR L at 356 and drum latex FOB at 246.
The INRO five-day average rose to 245.86 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Aug 27 from 245.30 on Aug 26. The daily indicator rose to 247.57 from 245.92. ($1=2.4930 ringgit)
